title: Budgets + Alerts Export: wireframe & grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures UX notes, wireframe annotations, and the grooming backlog for the budgets/alerts export flow in the Console billing area. Focus: make it simple for customers to 1) run ad-hoc exports for cost allocation and invoices, 2) schedule recurring exports (CSV/JSON), and 3) attach alert configuration snapshots for audits.

Problem context and goals:
- Customers frequently ask for exports that include allocation metadata (cost center tags, route/model breakdowns, token-level cost) for downstream finance systems.
- Current export is limited: single invoice export, poor filter UX, no schedule, no alert snapshot.
- Goal: Unified Export modal that supports ad-hoc + scheduled exports, selectable schema, and optional include of "alert snapshots" (current alert thresholds and recipients) for audits.
- Success metrics: reduce support tickets about CSV schema, increase scheduled-export usage by 3x for finance teams, <5% error rate on scheduled exports in first 90 days.

Primary user journeys (short):
1) Finance analyst: one-off export for month-end reconciliation. Steps: open Billing > Budgets, apply cost-center filter, choose invoice range, toggle "include allocations", export CSV.
2) Platform engineer: schedule nightly export with full token/cost breakdown to S3. Steps: Export modal -> Schedule -> Select format JSON (newline-delimited), provide S3 bucket + IAM role or signed URL -> Save.
3) Billing admin: export alert configuration for compliance. Steps: Budgets -> Alerts tab -> Export -> choose "Alert snapshot" -> includes threshold, channels, on-call rotation.

Wireframe summary (see Figma link in linked_artifacts):
- Main list: budgets table keeps existing columns; add a compact "Export" icon per-row for quick ad-hoc exports.
- Top-level toolbar: global Export button that opens multi-tab modal (Ad-hoc | Schedule | Alert snapshot).
- Modal layout: left column = filters summary (applied cost centers, projects, model, region, date range). Middle = schema builder (checkbox list of columns: date, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, unit_cost, cost, cost_center_tag, invoice_id). Right = preview pane (first 100 rows sample, dehydrated values for large KV fields).
- Export settings section (modal bottom): format selector (CSV/JSON/Parquet), compression (gzip/none), timezone selector, timezone-aware date ranges, file naming pattern (defaults: redwood-export-{org}-{yyyymmdd}), delivery options (download, S3, GCS, SFTP, signed-url email).
- Schedule tab: cron-friendly presets (Daily @ 00:00 UTC, Weekly Mon 00:00 UTC, Monthly 01 00:00 UTC), timezone dropdown, retry policy (3 attempts backoff), failure notifications (who to notify).
- Alert snapshot tab: single-click include of all active budget alerts with metadata, optional anonymize email addresses checkbox for compliance.

Important UX decisions / tradeoffs:
- Schema complexity vs. discoverability: default to a compact set of columns for ad-hoc users, require "Advanced schema" toggle to show token-level breakdowns to avoid overwhelming finance users.
- Delivery targets: support both push (S3/GCS/SFTP) and pull (signed URL). For push, we require a service-account flow: customers provide destination + signed trust relation or use a one-time upload endpoint.
- Export size: large exports will be prepared asynchronously; user gets email + console notification with signed URL. For scheduled exports: keep last 7 runs in console with status.

Edge cases and constraints:
- Very large date ranges ( > 90 days ) should warn about approximate results due to aggregation and sampling in the runtime.
- When including KV cache prefixes or prompt text, there are PII risks — add explicit opt-in and redaction guidance.
- Rate-limits: scheduled exports should be queued to avoid contention with serving runtime; include quota info in modal.
- Deleting a budget/alert should not retroactively delete past scheduled exports; record provenance metadata in export file header.

Open questions (to resolve before final sprint):
- Format for allocation mapping: do we prefer flat column names cost_center_1..cost_center_n or nested JSON column? (impact downstream ingestion; prefer JSON for rich mappings).
- Which auth model for push exports do we support on MVP? (S3 pre-signed URLs vs full cross-account IAM role).
- Should alert snapshots include historical throttling/firing history or only config? (privacy and size implications).

Grooming backlog (proposed tickets with rough sizing):
- CONSOLE-488: Export modal base UI + basic filters + ad-hoc CSV download (3). Priority: P0 for month-end customers.
- CONSOLE-489: Schema builder + preview pane + compact defaults (3). Priority: P0.
- CONSOLE-490: Scheduled exports backend + DB model + delivery to S3 via pre-signed URLs (5). Priority: P1.
- CONSOLE-491: Alert snapshot exporter + anonymize option (2). Priority: P1.
- CONSOLE-492: Large-export async job + signed URL notification flow (5). Priority: P0.
- CONSOLE-493: Compliance redaction flow + policy toggle for PII fields (3). Priority: P2.
- CONSOLE-494: UI for export run history + retry button (2). Priority: P1.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can perform ad-hoc exports for a single budget or filtered set and receive a CSV within 2 minutes for datasets under 100k rows.
- Users can create a scheduled export to S3 via pre-signed URL and see success/failure status in console.
- Alert snapshot includes threshold, channels, and recipient IDs, downloadable alongside data exports.
- Export schema is stable and documented in console help with an example file.

Accessibility & localisation notes:
- All inputs must have accessible labels; date-picker must support keyboard entry.
- Timezone behavior should be explicit (UTC default) and localize exported timestamps or include timezone field in file.

Monitoring / observability considerations:
- Instrument export requests with export_type, rows_estimate, delivery_target, created_by to help debug and to build SLA reports.
- Track scheduled export failure reasons (permissions, bucket not found, quota) for better UX.

Next steps / short-term plan:
- (This week) Align with backend on schema and payload limits (Ravi).
- (2 weeks) UX 2-up: compact vs advanced modal (Olivia) -> gather 3 customer feedback sessions (finance lead, platform eng, billing admin).
- (3 weeks) Groom and break down backlog tickets; set sprint priorities for M1 delivery (aim for ad-hoc + alert snapshot in first release).

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep the preview truncated to 100 rows and give a CSV column count in header.
- Consider including a small sample invoice_id checksum to help support match exports to billing events.
- For SFTP push, consider a managed intermediary (short term) to avoid building full SFTP credential flow.

——
Comments welcome: tag @Ravi for backend schema choices; @Olivia for microcopy and modal flows; @Dmitri for compliance redaction approach.
